ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, lines AB and CD intersect at point E, with EF$\perp$AB at point E. If $\angle FEC - \angle AEC = 20^\circ$, what is the measure of $\angle AED$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Let $\angle AEC$ be $x$, then $\angle FEC=x+20^\circ$. \\
Since EF$\perp$AB, \\
it follows that $\angle AEF=90^\circ$, \\
which means $\angle AEC+\angle FEC= 90^\circ$, \\
hence $x+x+20^\circ=90^\circ$, \\
Solving this gives: $x=35^\circ$, \\
that is $\angle AEC=35^\circ$, \\
Therefore, $\angle AED=180^\circ−35^\circ=\boxed{145^\circ}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, AB is a horizontal straight line, A is to the left of E, and B is to the right of E; CD is an oblique straight line, C is at the upper left of E, D is at the lower right of E, and C, E, D are collinear; EF goes vertically upward from E. It can be seen from the figure that EC is located between ray EA and EF, dividing angle AEF into two parts, ∠AEC and ∠FEC. Reasoning: Let ∠AEC = x. Because EF ⟂ AB, ∠AEF = 90°. Also because EC divides ∠AEF, ∠AEC + ∠FEC = 90°. The problem gives ∠FEC - ∠AEC = 20°, that is, ∠FEC = x + 20°. Therefore x + (x + 20°) = 90°, solving gives 2x = 70°, x = 35°, so ∠AEC = 35°. Since C, E, D are collinear, EC and ED are opposite rays, therefore ∠AEC and ∠AED form a linear adjacent supplementary angle, with sum 180°. So ∠AED = 180° - 35° = 145°.
